diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then equation \eqref{eq: lojasiewicz} holds for $\fv_{(k,i)}$ and together with \eqref{eq:function_increase}, we obtain

issues.failure_explanation: The Łojasiewicz inequality is stated for each block restriction F_i near v_*^{(i)}. F_i depends on the other blocks, which change with k, and F_i(v_*^{(i)}) is not F(v_*). The proof nevertheless inserts it as a bound of F(v_*)-F(v_(k,i)) by the Riemannian gradient of F_i at the current iterate. A block-coordinate adaptation of Schneider–Uschmajew needs the inequality for the full analytic F on the product of spheres. It also needs a bound relating the full gradient to the step lengths of all blocks, which is not given. The step bounded by 2Λ_i(G-G')/G^{θ_i} also drops the factor 1/(1-θ_i).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the argument with the Łojasiewicz inequality for the full F. Add the standard lemma bounding ||grad F|| by the sum of block step lengths, with the 1/(1-θ) constants. This follows the cited Schneider–Uschmajew template.
issues.overall_effect: Global convergence of the iterates (Cauchy property and algebraic rate) of PS-HOPM is not established as written. This also affects the global-convergence claim in the abstract and conclusion, and the global convergence claimed for the shifted tensor in the shift proposition.
issues.title: Łojasiewicz argument applied to block restrictions instead of the full objective
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is plausibly true and a known proof template exists. The repair is a contained but nontrivial new argument, not new global architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: h is decreasing in ν (h(2/3)=2/3, h(1)=0). Since F ≤ 1 always, ν=1 satisfies the stated hypothesis and gives γ_i=0 for all i. That would claim block convexity with no shift, which contradicts the purpose of the shifts. Monotone ascent of the iterates guarantees a lower bound F ≥ ν, not an upper bound, so the hypothesis is the wrong way round. As stated, the shift can be too small for iterates with larger F. The proof also defers the key bound to an external lemma. F is also ambiguous between F_A and the shifted F.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis as F ≥ ν along the iterates, ensured by initializing with F_A ≥ ν and monotone ascent. Make F in the hypothesis unambiguous (F_A versus the shifted F). Check the cited lemma gives the bound in that direction.
issues.overall_effect: The stated shifts do not ensure block convexity, and therefore global convergence, under the stated hypothesis.
issues.title: Shift in Proposition has the bound on F in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: A local change of hypothesis plus an initialization condition keeps the shift formula, the method and the conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since $\mathbf{H}_{1,1}$ is negative definite, being a submatrix of the Hessian at a maximizer.
and the negative definiteness of the Hessian of $F$.

issues.failure_explanation: A second-order critical point of a maximization has a negative semidefinite Riemannian Hessian. The proof uses strict negative definiteness for the bounds λ<1 and for eigenvalues of (JΨ_1)_{11} below 1. For degenerate maxima (e.g. repeated singular values giving a continuum of maximizers) the Jacobian can have eigenvalue 1, so the spectral radius is not <1 and the stated argument gives no linear rate.

failure_location.quote: has local linear convergence around every pSVT that is a second-order critical point of $F$ with positive singular value

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to pSVTs that are strict (nondegenerate) local maxima, i.e. with negative definite Riemannian Hessian. Alternatively, add a Morse–Bott argument for degenerate maxima.
issues.overall_effect: The local linear convergence guarantee is only established at nondegenerate local maximizers. The corresponding claim in the introduction and conclusion is overstated.
issues.title: Local linear convergence proved only for strict (negative definite) maxima, claimed for all second-order critical points
issues.why_classification: Restricting the hypothesis is a limited weakening, but it changes the advertised scope. The fully general version needs a new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: From <T_w,R^(i)> = μ_i + Σ_{j≠i} μ_j<R^(j),R^(i)> one gets |μ_i - <R^(i),T_w>| ≤ (r-1)ρ‖μ‖_∞, not ρ‖μ‖_∞, since there are r-1 cross terms. The correct bound is ‖μ‖_∞ ≤ max/(1-(r-1)ρ), valid only if (r-1)ρ<1. The constant C with (1-ρ)^{-1} is unsupported and can fail when the R^(i) are nearly dependent but have small pairwise inner products. No assumption (r-1)ρ<1 is stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1-ρ by 1-(r-1)ρ and assume (r-1)ρ<1 (or bound ‖μ‖ via the inverse Gram matrix). The theorem then holds with a modified constant.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound F_A ≤ C max|<R,T_w>| with the stated C, and the remark for ρ=0, are not established for the general parameter regime.
issues.title: Gram-matrix bound loses a factor (r-1); constant C and hypothesis are wrong
issues.why_classification: The fix changes the constant and adds a hypothesis, giving a comparable but weaker result via a contained re-derivation.

issues.failure_explanation: Replacing the exponent ℓf_j by 2 uses |x|^{ℓf_j} ≤ |x|^2, which needs ℓf_j ≥ 2 and |x| ≤ 1. The paper allows f_j=0 (e.g. f=(1,1,0)). Then the term equals Σ_i 1 = r, not ≤ Σ|<v_i,w>|^2 ≤ 1+(r-1)ρ_j. The block's ρ_j is irrelevant to F_A because that factor does not occur in R^(i). So the product formula for C is invalid; ℓ=1, f=1 would also fail.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the product to blocks with f_j>0, handle blocks with f_j=0 via the factor r^{1/ℓ} (or an adjusted Hölder split), and correct the constant and the remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated constant C, and the ρ=0 remark giving F_A ≤ max|<R,T_w>|, are unsupported for flattenings with some f_j=0, which the paper uses.
issues.title: Exponent step requires ℓ f_j ≥ 2; fails for blocks with f_j = 0
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation, but the constant changes (extra r-dependent factor) and the clean remark is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the vectors $\fv_{i}^{(j)}$ are generic with norm one, and assume $\dim \Acal = r$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes only genericity and dim A = r, but the proof's uniqueness step needs r ≤ r(f), which is never stated. Moreover A is defined as a span of rank-one tensors with exponents d_j, whereas r(f) controls rank-one tensors in the f-flattened space. The proof then treats T'⊗R_(f) ∈ A as forcing T' to be a complement R^(j)_(d-f), without relating the d-level span to the f-level uniqueness. Without r ≤ r(f), other rank-one elements exist and uniqueness fails.

failure_location.quote: are the only rank-one elements in $\Acal$ (up to scale), since $r \leq r(f)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r ≤ r(f) (and the needed r(d-f) conditions) to the statement. Rewrite the proof with consistent spaces (S^{f} versus S^{d}), showing T'⊗R_(f) in the right span forces a known summand.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniqueness of the complement as the only rank-one singular vector of M is unsupported as stated. The recovery rank formulas in the corollary inherit this.
issues.title: Match-up theorem uses r ≤ r(f) without assuming it and conflates the spaces for d and f
issues.why_classification: The result is probably true with the right hypotheses. The proof needs a contained reorganization, not a new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For f=(1,1), d=(4,1), k=2, the theorem gives r(f)=min{C(n+2,3), (n-1)(k-1)+1}=min{C(n+2,3), n}=n. The corollary's proof states min{4,n}, which differs for n≥5. The error does not change the conclusion, since (2,1) dominates anyway.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace min{4,n} by n for k=2. The stated dominance conclusion is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed intermediate value in the proof is wrong. The final optimal-tuple statement is unaffected.
issues.title: Formula for r(1,1) at ℓ=4, k=2 contradicts Theorem on r(f)
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction consistent with Theorem 4.2 preserves all claims.

issues.failure_explanation: Write C^{-1}=AΛB^T with columns α_i=U^T vec(R_(f)^i), β_i=V^T vec(R_(d-f)^i). Then β_1^T C α_i=0 for i≥2, so α_i⊥C^T a_v, and β_i⊥C a_u. Hence Û=U O_v needs O_v ⊥ C^T a_v. With O_v ⊥ C a_v, as written, the columns of Û need not contain the vectors α_i (i≥2), and (b),(c) fail for nonsymmetric C (C is r×r with U,V of different row spaces when f≠d-f). The same formula is used in the deflation step of Algorithm MSPM.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define O_v as an orthonormal basis of Span{C^T a_v}^⊥ in the proposition and in the algorithm's deflation step; the rest is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The deflated factorization in (b),(c) and the deflation step of the MSPM algorithm are incorrect unless C is symmetric.
issues.title: Deflation: orthogonal complement should use C^T a_v, not C a_v
issues.why_classification: A single local substitution restores (a)–(c) with the same method and guarantees.
